description: The fifth analysis kind, and it exists because this weakness has no call and no comparison in it: the caller's claim is simply moved to the far side of a trust boundary. Everything downstream reads the session back as state the server established, and by then the fact that a caller chose it is gone. The IR recorded assignments to plain names and nothing else until this needed them, so a write into a property was not merely undetected but unexpressible.

expected.note: the caller's claim becomes server-side state

the same line, read by a second rule and answering a different question: the claim is the caller's AND the identifier that names the session was not rotated. Two defects, two fixes, and neither one repairs the other

a fixture's negatives are negatives for the rule it was written for. This line is the right answer to the trust-boundary question and still installs an identity without rotating the session identifier
